references.text: God reveals Himself to Jacob in Bethel and gives him promises, which are renewed upon his return to Bethel.
God blesses Jacob and gives him the name Israel at Peniel, a fact confirmed again in Gen 35:10.
The context of God's revelation: Jacob returns to Bethel after God's command and purifies his household.
Jacob recalls that God Almighty revealed Himself to him in Luz (Bethel) and blessed him—a direct reference to this event.
God reveals Himself to Abraham and blesses Him with promises—a pattern repeated with Jacob in Bethel.
Jeremiah theologically confirms that Jacob's blessing in Genesis is part of God's eternal redemption and saving act.
The psalm interprets Jacob's historical turning point and blessing as an expression of God's eternal goodwill and reversal of fate.
Jacob refers directly back to the same revelation event (Luz/Bethel) to confirm God's faithfulness over time.
The psalm builds its theology on God's help upon the historical revelation and the identity 'the God of Jacob' established in Genesis.
